messages:
pagerduty-bot: [P1] High tail latency detected for inference egress across multiple regions (eu-west1, ap-south2). Alert triggered: latency > 1.5s p95 for 2m. Paging oncall-ryan.

oncall-ryan: saw it. investigating. are we seeing error rates increase or just latency?

sre-ana: p95 up, error rate steady. traces point to egress NAT saturation on eu-west1 and ap-south2 edge POPs. KV cache hitrate fine.

infra-lin: confirmed NAT pool exhaustion on eu-west1-zoneb based on vpc-nat metrics. ap-south2 has intermittent path flaps to our peering.

oncall-ryan: ok starting mitigation. plan: 1) reroute new requests away from affected POPs, 2) throttle bursty non-prod clients, 3) update status page draft. handing to ana to coordinate routing.

sre-ana: applying routing policy now: divert region-pref traffic for eu-west1 -> eu-central1 and ap-south2 -> ap-southeast1. executing route change.

infra-lin: routing change applied via router-control. commands used:```bash
# divert 10% incremental to fallback
routerctl update-policy --name egress-pref --from eu-west1 --to eu-central1 --pct 100
routerctl update-policy --name egress-pref --from ap-south2 --to ap-southeast1 --pct 100
```

ops-bot: announce: routing policy updated. observing metrics for 2 minutes.

product-zoe: customers on Dedicated might still hit local egress; add note to customer notification about possible brief degraded latency for pinned deployments.

customer-ops-julia: drafting customer-facing blurb, sharing below for quick review. please comment:```
Subject: Brief service degradation affecting inference latency in EU and AP regions

Hi — we detected elevated latency for API requests routed through specific edge locations in EU (eu-west1) and AP (ap-south2). We have diverted traffic to nearby healthy regions and are seeing improvements.

Impact: increased latency for a small portion of requests (p95 ~1.5-2s) and potential transient errors for connections mid-swap.

Mitigation: traffic has been routed to eu-central1 and ap-southeast1. No data loss. If you have Dedicated capacity pinned to affected POPs, our team will reach out with guidance.

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2045554321

We will update as we have more details. Sorry for the disruption.
```

oncall-ryan: LGTM, can we include a line for how customers can opt into immediate region pinning fallback? ana can add.

sre-ana: added instructions for Dedicated customers and runbook snippet. internal short status for slack:```
INCIDENT (P1) — egress NAT saturation in eu-west1 & peering flaps in ap-south2. Traffic diverted to eu-central1 & ap-southeast1. Mitigation in progress, monitoring. Action: routing diversion, throttle non-prod bursters, reach out to Dedicated customers. Owners: ana (triage), lin (infra), ryan (commms).```

infra-lin: monitoring shows drop in p95 after diversion: eu-west1 p95 -> 350ms (from 1.8s), ap-south2 -> 420ms (from 1.6s). still watching.

ops-bot: statuspage: proposed update posted to staging. URL: https://status.redwood.ai/draft/2045554321

product-zoe: need a clear internal template for SOC and CSM teams to use when contacting customers. Julia, can you add CSM checklist?

customer-ops-julia: pasted CSM checklist below for people to copy/send:```
Hi [Customer],
We saw transient latency affecting requests routed via [eu-west1|ap-south2]. We have temporarily routed traffic to a healthy POP (eu-central1 or ap-southeast1).
- Impact: elevated latency for a subset of requests for ~10-30 minutes.
- Action taken: routing change + throttling of noisy non-prod clients.
- Next steps: we will confirm when original egress is healthy and offer to re-pin traffic.
- Contact: support@redwood.ai (include incident id 2045554321)
```

oncall-ryan: quick note for on-call handoff in ~30m: if latency remains >500ms p95 in any region, escalate to exec-ops and open a customer-wide notification. For now, keep monitoring and post updates every 10m.

sre-ana: internal mitigation checklist completed: reroute applied, cache warmup triggered, non-prod throttles enacted. running follow-up:```bash
# warm KV cache for common prefixes
for prefix in $(cat hot_prompts.txt); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d \"{\"prompt\": \"$prefix\"}\" & done
```

infra-lin: FYI we also cleared a small NAT leak by increasing ephemeral SNAT pool on eu-west1 for now:```bash
gcloud compute routers nats update nat-eu-west1 --min-ports-per-vm 128 --udp-timeout 30s
```

ops-bot: monitoring update: overall API errors stable, p95 trending down.

product-zoe: thanks team. can someone drop a short internal blurb for #general? needs to be two lines max.

oncall-ryan: posting internal blurb (copy): \"FYI: brief latency spike impacting eu & ap regions. Traffic diverted to healthy POPs; mitigation in progress, no data loss. Updates every 10m. (incident 2045554321)\"

customer-ops-julia: final customer note ready to send in 10m if metrics stay good.

sre-ana: handing off monitoring to lin for the 30m window, i'm off to handle postmortem skeleton and evals to capture regression tests.

infra-lin: taking over monitoring. will escalate if any relapse.

oncall-ryan: thanks all, oncall handoff to infra-lin at 2045554600 confirmed. next update at 2045554705.

ops-bot: handoff recorded: from oncall-ryan -> infra-lin at 2045554600.

infra-lin: last note — recommend we add automated fallback policy for NAT saturation to the Optimize recommendations: auto-divert when SNAT utilization >85%. filing ticket: https://github.com/redwood-internal/infra/issues/6421

sre-ana: ack. adding to post-incident action items. closing thread when metrics stable for 30m.
